paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is about. God brings a charge against Israel, and the charge is about a people who talk big and live crooked. Ephraim "surrounds Me with lies," boasts about his riches, and uses "dishonest scales" while saying nobody can find any sin in him (Hosea 11:12; 12:7-8). That's a box marked a dozen with TEN cookies inside and a smile on the label.

Now look at what Jacob's story is doing here. Jacob grabbed and wrestled and ran, but he also "wept and sought His favor," and he found God at Bethel (Hosea 12:3-4). Then comes the call: "But you must return to your God; maintain love and justice, and always wait on your God" (Hosea 12:6). I think the point is that you don't fix a crooked life by getting stronger or richer. You fix it by turning back to God and letting your hands match your words.

And friend, notice who has been faithful the whole time. God says, "I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt," and He says He spoke through the prophets and multiplied their visions (Hosea 12:9-10). He brought Israel out of Egypt and preserved them by a prophet (Hosea 12:13). So when God's Word gets in your ear, that's not Him picking on you. That's Him calling you back, and I'd say yes to that call before the oven timer goes off.
